name: Apple
title: Buy Idea: Price Target $300–$350
guidance: FY2026 revenue guidance: ~$478.7B vs Street at higher estimates
FY2026 EPS guidance: ~$8.74 vs Street at higher estimates
drivers: Dominant ecosystem (hardware, software & services) driving retention and pricing power.
Capital-light on-device AI (Apple Intelligence) protects margins vs. hyperscaler AI capex peers.
Services hit record revenue in FY26 Q2, expected to drive continued margin mix improvement.
Record March quarter on iPhone 17 demand; Greater China revenue +28% YoY.
New Broadcom chip supply deal (>$30B through 2031) secures custom silicon, de-risks supply chain.
John Ternus (Hardware SVP) succeeds Tim Cook as CEO after the Q3 FY26 call — planned transition.
financial_health: Last Q recap: Rev $111.2B (+17% YoY, record) vs $109.7B Street. EPS (GAAP) $2.01 (+22% YoY).
This Q expectation: Rev +14–17% YoY. EPS +~20% YoY.
Debt-to-equity ~70–80%, as Apple generates very strong free cash flow (~$129B TTM) to manage debt effectively.
performance: Mid-term performance: +22% YTD at the time of writing; reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company from Nvidia.
Long-term performance: multi-year uptrend intact on ecosystem durability & services mix shift.
competition: Faces increasing competition from Samsung and Chinese OEMs (Huawei, Xiaomi) in smartphones.
Maintains strong partnerships with carriers and global retail/online distribution channels.
Heavily reliant on TSMC for manufacturing and Foxconn/Pegatron for assembly; memory-chip shortage could pose challenges.
management: CEO: Tim Cook — CEO since 2011; visionary leader driving Apple's ecosystem growth.
Incoming CEO: John Ternus (previously SVP Hardware Engineering), effective after the Q3 FY26 call.
risks: Valuation: trading at high multiples (~35–41x); potential corrections.
China tariffs & export restrictions could impact sales & sourcing costs.
Fed interest rates: macro risk for growth stocks.
Execution risk: CEO transition to John Ternus.
Supply chain: TSMC/Foxconn concentration; memory-chip shortage raising costs.
news_sentiment: Overall positive: the Broadcom supply deal & Apple reclaiming the world's-most-valuable-company title.
Concerns: an App Store lawsuit and a dispute with Chinese memory suppliers.
ownership: Insiders have skewed toward selling in the past 3 months, typical for large-cap executives.
bottom_line: Apple's ecosystem leadership, capital-light AI strategy and strong Services growth make it a top pick, despite valuation risks and the pending CEO transition which could impact sentiment.
valuation: This year EPS growth: 17% vs S&P 12%
Next year EPS growth: 9.5% vs S&P 12%
valuation_bottom_line: Strong ecosystem economics and record Services growth justify a premium valuation. Forecast 0%–15% upside, targeting $300–$350, based on continued Services momentum and a well-managed leadership transition.
catalysts_to_watch: Q3 FY26 results & CEO transition to John Ternus.
